sources.quote: friends or family were the most common source, ahead of banks, investment firms and insurers
sources.title: Survey findings offer glimpse into how Canadians seek financial advice - Canada.ca
sources.evidence: Friends or family were the most popular source of advice, followed by banks, investment firms, insurance providers, and professional advisors. Survey respondents were most likely to seek advice from friends or family members (37%) or from trusted organizations like banks, investment companies or insurance providers (33%). Other common sources of financial advice were professional financial advisors or planners (25%).

sources.quote: the Securities and Investment Management Association reported record mutual fund assets of about $2.53 trillion at the end of 2025, up roughly 13% year over year, on net sales of $40.5 billion
sources.publisher: Securities and Investment Management Association (SIMA) via Cision Newswire
sources.title: SIMA releases 2025 Annual Statistics Report
sources.evidence: Mutual fund assets under management rose to $2.53 trillion by year end – an increase of 12.7 per cent year over year. Mutual fund net sales totalled $40.5 billion in 2025 – more than double the 2024 level. SIMA released its 2025 Annual Statistics Report on January 28, 2026.

sources.quote: Rule 3600 governs advertisements, sales literature and correspondence: Part A requires pre-approval, and the dealer must retain what was published plus the supervision records
sources.title: Guidelines for the review, supervision and retention of advertisements, sales literature and correspondence | Canadian Investment Regulatory Organization
sources.evidence: Rule 3600 is divided into three parts: Part A covers advertisements, sales literature and correspondence (sections 3602 and 3603). Under subsection 3603(6), a Dealer must retain copies of all advertisements, sales literature and correspondence and all records of supervision. Original advertising and any material that is used to solicit clients must be subject to pre-use approval for both content and disclosure requirements.

sources.quote: CSA and CIRO Staff Notice 31-369, published December 11, 2025, covers finfluencers
sources.publisher: Canadian Investment Regulatory Organization (CIRO) and Canadian Securities Administrators (CSA)
sources.title: Joint Canadian Securities Administrators and Canadian Investment Regulatory Organization Staff Notice 31-369 Guidance on the Application of Securities Legislation to Finfluencer Activity | Canadian Investment Regulatory Organization
sources.evidence: The CSA and CIRO published Joint Staff Notice 31-369 Guidance on The Application of Securities Legislation to Finfluencer Activity on December 11, 2025. This staff notice provides guidance on how securities laws apply to the activities of social media financial influencers (finfluencers) and to registrants and issuers who work with them.

sources.quote: FP Canada reports roughly 17,000 CFP professionals
sources.title: Home | FP Canada
sources.evidence: There are about 17,300 CFP professionals across Canada. CFP professionals in Canada are certified by FP Canada, a national, not-for-profit professional body working in the public interest.

sources.quote: The CFP and QAFP marks may never appear in a firm name, domain name or email address
sources.title: CFP Marks Usage Guide
sources.evidence: The CFP Marks may not be used as part of the name of a firm or other business entity. The companion QAFP Marks Usage Guide states the QAFP marks may not be used as part of a domain name or as part of an email address.

sources.quote: for the 2025 tax year it fell on Monday, March 2, 2026
sources.title: Important dates for RRSPs, HBP, LLP, FHSAs and more - Canada.ca
sources.evidence: March 2, 2026 is the deadline for contributing to an RRSP for the 2025 tax year. Contributions made to your RRSP, PRPP or SPP or your spouse's RRSP or SPP from March 4, 2025 to March 2, 2026 qualify.

sources.quote: its advisor transition window closing March 28, 2024 and its planner window March 28, 2026
sources.publisher: Financial Services Regulatory Authority of Ontario (FSRA)
sources.title: Transition | Financial Services Regulatory Authority of Ontario
sources.evidence: The transition period for using the Financial Advisor (or similar) title concluded on March 28, 2024. The transition period for using the Financial Planner (or similar) title in Ontario will conclude on March 28, 2026. The transition period only applies if you were using the Financial Planner title on or before January 1, 2020.

sources.quote: New Brunswick's came into force January 1, 2026 under the Financial and Consumer Services Commission, phased in over two years for advisors and four for planners
sources.publisher: Financial and Consumer Services Commission of New Brunswick (FCNB)
sources.title: Financial Advisors and Financial Planners | New Brunswick Financial and Consumer Services Commission
sources.evidence: The Financial Advisors and Financial Planners Title Protection Act came into force on January 1, 2026. The transition periods – two years for financial advisors and four years for financial planners – give individuals time to comply with the framework.

sources.quote: Implied consent from an inquiry lasts six months
sources.publisher: Innovation, Science and Economic Development Canada (ISED)
sources.title: Getting consent to send email
sources.evidence: Implied consent may be valid for up to 2 years—or just 6 months in the case of inquiries or applications. Every unsubscribe request must be actioned within 10 business days or less and at no cost to the recipient.
